name: Villanueva de la Cañada & Mosquito Ridge
story: Villanueva de la Cañada, held by a small Nationalist garrison, resisted the Republican offensive through the first day at Brunete and fell only on the night of 7 July, after the XV International Brigade and other units had been pinned in the open wheatfields. North-east of the village, the Republican drive towards Boadilla stalled on the Mosquito Ridge (Loma de los Mosquitos), where the British and American battalions suffered heavily in repeated attacks under a scorching sun. The failure to take the ridge ended hopes of cutting the Nationalist lines west of Madrid.
see: A modern town; the ridge line and open country of the battle are visible from the Villanueva del Pardillo–Boadilla area, with scattered fortifications.
plan: Best seen by car from the M-600 and M-503 roads; no dedicated interpretation on site.
